html:
A wave of Protestant revival that swept through Britain's North American colonies, peaking in the late 1730s and 1740s. Preachers called on people to feel their sinfulness and experience a personal rebirth, not just attend church.

Its leading voices:

  • Jonathan Edwards, a minister in Massachusetts, whose sermon "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God" (1741) is still famous.
  • George Whitefield, an English preacher and friend of the Methodist John Wesley, who toured the colonies from 1739 and preached outdoors to crowds of thousands.

The revival split churches into "New Lights", who backed it, and "Old Lights", who distrusted its emotion. It led to new colleges, such as the one that became Princeton. It also brought many enslaved and free Black people into Protestant churches for the first time.

Because it was the first movement that touched all the colonies at once, some historians see it as a step toward a shared American identity before the Revolution. The older Puritan churches of the Puritan settlers never fully recovered their hold.
sum: A wave of Protestant revival that swept through Britain's North American colonies, peaking in the late 1730s and 1740s. Preachers called on people to feel their sinfulness and experience a personal rebirth, not just attend church.
